title: "Life never handed me lemons. It handed me…": your funniest flaw
summary: Start with "Life never handed me lemons. It handed me…" and finish it with a harmless flaw or bad habit. AI helps you find the funniest ending.
why: SocialBee's latest Instagram trends post, dated November 5, 2026, lists "Life never handed me lemons. It handed me…" as a new Reels trend: a text overlay that sets up the old saying, then lands on a funny flaw or bad habit.
steps: Use the main prompt to get a list of endings that fit you.
Film a short, ordinary clip that matches the ending: your messy desk, your fifth coffee, the pile of laundry on the chair.
Add the text "Life never handed me lemons. It handed me…" first, then reveal the ending a beat later.
Keep it 5 to 8 seconds so people watch it twice.

prompts.label: Main prompt
prompts.text: Help me with a short Reel. The on-screen text starts "Life never handed me lemons. It handed me…" and ends with a harmless flaw or bad habit of mine, said in a funny, self-aware way. Write 12 endings, under 12 words each. For example: "a phone at 3% and a strong will to ignore it." About me: [your habits, quirks, job, hobbies]. Keep it light and kind. Nothing about health, money troubles or other people.

prompts.label: Variation: match the clip
prompts.text: I've already filmed this clip: [describe it, for example: me hunting for my keys for the third time this morning]. Write 6 "Life never handed me lemons. It handed me…" endings that fit what's on screen. Then pick the strongest one and tell me where in the clip the ending should appear.

prompts.label: Variation: pets
prompts.text: Write 8 "Life never handed me lemons. It handed me…" endings from my pet's point of view. My pet: [type, name, habits, for example: a cat who sits on every keyboard]. Keep them playful and short, under 12 words each.

prompts.label: Variation: small business
prompts.text: I run [type of business] in [town]. Write 8 "Life never handed me lemons. It handed me…" endings about the funny, honest side of running it: the odd requests, the tiny workspace, the 6 a.m. starts. Each one should feel friendly, not like a complaint, and never poke fun at customers. Suggest a simple behind-the-scenes shot for each. Don't invent sales, numbers or customer quotes.

tips: Pick a flaw people will recognise in themselves. Relatable beats clever.
Pause before the ending. The short gap is where the laugh comes from.
Keep it about you, not someone else. Gentle self-teasing is the whole point.
Business accounts may not have the trending sound. An original sound works fine.
